advice: Propose an outer loop over the existing 32-row panel helper’s packing and 16-column-tile compute blocks, with one SME entry/exit and one 64 KiB scratch allocation for the full n=512 call. For each row band r=0,32,…,480, set A to A+r*512, B to the original B base, and C to C+r*512; pack that band, compute all 512 columns, then advance to the next band. Keep the helper’s inner K loops, FP32 operation order, stores, and general-size fallback unchanged. This is a distinct wrapper/body traversal change from the measured sixteen-call wrapper: it aims to reduce repeated call and SME transition overhead while retaining the same panel packing and arithmetic. Treat any benefit as unverified; the scores do not establish a cache bottleneck or that transition overhead is material. The editable helper’s reported feasibility review describes the required pointer resets and scratch lifetime, but implementation needs careful assembly and ABI review.
risks: A single-entry loop must preserve callee-saved registers and stack alignment, keep the 64 KiB scratch allocated while compute reads it, reset B and C tile pointers for each band, and cover every output row exactly once. A pointer or stack-lifetime error can corrupt output. All sixteen packs and tile traversals remain timed, so fewer SME transitions may not offset added loop control. Preserve the full LIBXSMM BSD notice and unchanged fallback. Check a byte-identical helper round trip before editing behavior, then compile with the fixed flags and run full-GEMM correctness at tolerance 0.002, including n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0, output overwrite, and unchanged-input checks. Measure fresh repeated paired controls on the block’s unchanged power source and settings; report spread and do not infer causality from noisy scores.
